literal_source_claim: 非一致双曲理论 (nonuniform hyperbolic theory)
statement_blocker: The repository supplies only a theory label and broad field gloss. It does not select a dynamical system, regularity and measure hypotheses, a meaning of nonuniform hyperbolicity, almost-everywhere and boundary conventions, or one theorem conclusion. Selecting a standard Pesin result would substitute missing mathematics.
domain_and_universes: Open: an exact source must fix a finite-dimensional smooth or Riemannian phase space and universes, compactness and boundary conditions, a diffeomorphism, noninvertible map, or flow, its regularity, and invariant measure data.
conclusion: Open: the source names a theory but states no truth-valued result about Pesin blocks, invariant manifolds, absolute continuity, closing or ergodic consequences, or entropy.
candidate_scope_not_credited: a source-specified nonuniform stable and unstable manifold theorem for almost every regular point
a source-specified theorem constructing or exhausting the regular set by Pesin blocks
a source-specified absolute-continuity theorem for stable or unstable laminations
a source-specified closing, shadowing, homoclinic, local-ergodicity, or Bernoulli consequence
a source-specified entropy theorem under exact smoothness and measure hypotheses
degenerate_cases_to_resolve: empty or null regular set and zero-dimensional phase spaces
zero Lyapunov exponents and trivial stable or unstable subspaces
atomic, singular, or nonergodic invariant measures
noncompact manifolds and integrability or recurrence failures
one-sided noninvertible maps versus two-sided diffeomorphisms or flows
empty Pesin blocks, zero local-manifold radii, and strict positivity of contraction constants
pointwise, almost-everywhere, blockwise-uniform, local, and global quantifier scopes
excluded_substitutions: THM-M-1346 the generic stable manifold theorem
THM-M-1411 uniform or general hyperbolic dynamical systems and THM-M-1412 Anosov diffeomorphisms
a definition of nonuniform hyperbolicity without a theorem conclusion
a finite-dimensional linear example, numerical Lyapunov computation, or generic ergodic/manifold API lemma
a structure that assumes the desired invariant manifolds, estimates, absolute continuity, or conclusion as fields
